newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market sees spate of fresh inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market sees spate of fresh inquiry.

text.p: The sugar freight market was awash with a spate of fresh inquiry but no fixtures at the start of the week, although shipbrokers continued to complain about falling rates over the whole of the dry cargo market.
"The rates are ghastly across the market -- it's really depressing," said one broker on Monday.
Earlier, the Baltic Freight Index (BFI) of charter rates on key world shipping routes dropped below 1,000 points for the first time in almost a decade.
The index dropped to 997, a fall of four points from last week. It had not been below 1,000 since August 4, 1987.
E D & F Man was active in the day's quoted new business, launching a number of inquiries for bagged sugar.
It quoted for 15,000 tonnes from Gdynia and Gdansk to Awaba for October 7/10 and a further 2,000 tonnes min/max from Gdynia or Rostock to Ploce or Thessaloniki for September 30/October 3.

Market sources said the Polish orders were likely to be related to the expiry of the October white sugar contract, when Man was the receiver of 266 lots, or 13,300 tonnes, from the ports of Gdynia and Gdansk.
Man was also in the market for 12,000 tonnes min/max from east coast India to Indonesia with Colombo option for October 1/10 and 6,000 tonnes from Rio de Janeiro to Colombo for October 15/20.
Man quoted for 3,000 tonnes min/max pre-slung bagged sugar from Cadiz to Lattakia or Tartous for spot/prompt dates.
Louis Dreyfus quoted for 14,300 tonnes of bagged sugar from Santos to the Red Sea for October 4/10
Vitol was open for 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from north Brazil to Casablanca with Black Sea option for October 7/15.
Shyvers Savoy quoted an account order for 10,000 tonnes in bags from Rio de Janeiro or Santos to Abidjan/Dakar range for October 1/10.

Fiji Sugar Marketing issued a new order after its fixture at the end of last week. It was open for 15,500 tonnes of bulk sugar from Fiji to Japan for October 20/30 and shipbrokers said the order would achieve a rate in the region of $22 or $23.
Secretan was open with six orders for bagged sugar from varying origins.
It quoted for 2,000 tonnes from Le Havre to Tallinn and 1,600 tonnes pre-slung from Cadiz to Algeria, both prompt, and 2/3,000 tonnes from Dunkirk to Batumi for Sept 26/Oct 5.

Secretan was also open for 10,500 tonnes from Recife to Abidjan for October 20/30, 22,500 tonnes from Santos to Dubai for October 1/7 and 10,000 tonnes from Madras to Continent and options for October 10/15.
